contract.claim: ExploreFrontier lists observed footing within a horizontal radius (default 128): stood means you stood there; seen_surface means a block you saw below your eye, one per 16-block sector. Its top face may not have been the face you saw, and whether it can be stood on, has headroom or sits beside lava is unknown until you get close. A surface later seen changed or covered is dropped. Each row gives dy (height change from your feet), horizontal distance and compass heading (north is -Z, east is +X); visited, blocked (a recent failure there) and ageS (seconds since that spot was last observed, only when old) mark uncertainty. Rows are ordered one per heading per round, farthest first; continue with offset (each call reads fresh facts, so pages can shift). coverage summarizes this world and dimension: blocks travelled, descended and climbed (sums between sampled footholds, so at least that much; deaths and teleports are not travel), your first remembered position, and for each heading [walked, seen] as the farthest blocks from you, followed by [sight range, age in seconds] when a complete survey taken within 32 blocks of you had that heading in its view cone (pitch counts: looking straight down covers no heading). The sight range is how far that view could reach (water and lava fog shorten it), not how far was searched: terrain and unloaded chunks hide what lies behind them, and a survey that found nothing proves nothing is there. Remembered structure and portal sightings follow. blockId instead pages remembered blocks of that exact id. It never chooses or travels; choose coordinates with moveTo. Survey results carry the same coverage as search, and coverage.rangeBlocks when fog shortened the view. moveTo results add travel when your height changed: feetDy (exact change of your feet), descendedAtLeast and climbedAtLeast (ground changes between sampled footholds), lowestGroundY (lowest sampled foothold), and startOnGround/endOnGround (false, or unknown) when you were not seen standing. NO_STANDABLE_PATH adds knownFooting, the nearest observed footing to the target with blocked and ageS. Stored places are scoped to world and dimension and can become stale.

contract.claim: A standing order is a reflex you author once, for danger faster than a model turn. `standing:{id,when,ttlS}` stores the source instead of running it; `when` is one side-effect-free expression over the same facts as a queueProgram precondition. The moment it turns true (or if it is true when stored) the source starts as a background program. It cancels your own running action or a program paused for your decision; a running program keeps the body, since its own watchers answer first. Its source must declare `{ survival: "continue_and_notify" }`, because urgent danger otherwise pauses a program, and an order runs during exactly that danger. It fires again only after the condition was false. At most four orders; each expires after `ttlS` seconds (default 600, at most 1800) and survives death and respawn. Every firing returns as a program result whose `standingOrder` names the order, the facts that fired it (`cause`) and what it `preempted`. A condition naming a fact absent from a sample reads false and shows `conditionError` in the order list. `standing:{id}` alone deletes the order.

A stance is not progress when the body keeps losing health: a stance that hits `maxS` after losing 2+ health counts as a failed firing and wakes you, and one held for three `maxS` spans in a row without its condition clearing wakes you once; give fleeing (`sprint_away`, `take_cover` on `health_below`) a higher priority than holding.

A firing takes the body from the running action, which pauses (it is not cancelled) and resumes when the firing ends; your program keeps waiting on that action. Health lost under the firing is the firing's: a resumed travel_to or navigate_to does not stop for it and travel_to plans its next leg from where the body now stands. The action's result names the rules that paused it (`paused 1 time(s) by reflex <id> for 0.4 s, resumed 1 time(s)`). A held `shield` lets a walking action (move_to, navigate_to, follow_entity, control, wait) keep moving behind it at vanilla's shield-raised speed (a fifth of walking), and inside `fight_target` the fight raises the offhand shield between its own swings except while a shot is about to land; `flee_from` takes the body from the shield and runs with it lowered. Each firing lasts at most `maxS` (default 4 s trigger, 10 s stance, at most 20; shield stances default to 600 s and accept maxS up to 600), then waits `cooldownS` (default 0.5). A rule expires after `ttlS` (default 600, at most 3600), when all its `until` conditions hold, or after `maxFirings`. `lasts` ties it to a context instead: `"night"` ends it at the first dawn (armed by day, it lasts the coming night), `"dimension"` when you leave the dimension it was armed in (a death elsewhere counts), `"lava"` once no lava has been within 12 blocks for a minute; with `lasts` and no `ttlS` the ttl is 3600. Wake lines name a rule's remaining seconds in its last 120 s and list expired rules with the reason. Four firings in a row without progress (failed, or a trigger hitting maxS), or more than 40 in a minute, disable the rule and wake you.
- Reports: every firing ends as done, hit maxS, failed, preempted, yielded, expired or DISABLED with a detail ("blocked 3 hit(s)", "no pickaxe in hotbar (2 in inventory)", "lost 4.0 health"). Precedence: your direct command, then a firing reflex, then a guard: a guard whose condition becomes true while a reflex fires waits for the firing to end and fires only if its condition still holds. You chose to fight: the body selects the best hotbar weapon (sword > axe/spear > other tool), turns, closes to reach and swings at 90%+ attack charge. Within reach a pursuing fight moves like a player between your calls: while the sword recharges it stays just outside the target's own melee reach and steps in, sprinting, as the charge completes (a sprint hit knocks the target back); against a living target with headroom it jumps so the charged swing lands while falling (a critical, x1.5; never on a dragon part, which takes no criticals); it circles the target, changing side irregularly so shots aimed where you stood miss, never onto unsafe footing; a projectile about to hit that your raised shield does not face is side-stepped; with a seen drop of 5+ blocks, the void or lava behind you within a hit's push it circles away from that side and never steps back; at low health (6, or fleeAtHealth+4) it keeps out of reach and stops jumping. Against the dragon it does not circle (its wings throw anyone beside or behind it). Results add `footwork` counts (crits, sprint hits, dodged shots, time circling off a drop). pursue:false keeps all of it off. The fight ends when the named target dies or is gone; pass `continueWithAttackers:true` (or a `targetPolicy`) to go on to the next mob already attacking you (never a creeper, never one that is not attacking) until none remain. The approach plans only over terrain you have seen: `TARGET_UNREACHABLE` means the whole area you can walk was seen and none of it reaches; with no route through seen terrain (one may exist out of sight), it holds position and swings if the target enters clear melee reach, until your timeout or bail-out; FIGHT_TIMED_OUT reports NO_SEEN_ROUTE and geometry if it remained waiting. With a held pearl, snowball or egg, inspect first via use_item `mode:"inspect"` with the same aim, then choose whether to throw. Each row gives dy (height change from your feet), horizontal distance and compass heading (north is -Z, east is +X); visited, blocked (a recent failure there) and ageS (seconds since that spot was last observed, only when old) mark uncertainty. Sprints away from the target and every other hostile threat within 16 blocks (nearer ones and creepers, especially swelling ones, push hardest), jumping steps and steering around walls, hazards and deep drops, until at least `distance` away and the target is not closing (`ESCAPED`), it lost you (`TARGET_LOST`), it is gone (`TARGET_GONE`, a failed result with last/best separation, never proof of escape), `FLEE_BLOCKED` (all tested headings failed) or `FLEE_TIMED_OUT`. It probes all 12 headings in 30-degree steps, including backtracking out of a dead end, with one-block jumps/step-ups. A physically stalled heading is excluded and alternatives tried before FLEE_BLOCKED; moving 1.5 blocks resets those exclusions. Results include moved distance, best separation and tried headings. Ending while still swimming, the result gives your air and the land you can see (nearest first); choose where to swim. Navigation stops at its destination; flee_from checks separation while threats keep moving. You choose the trade-off.

contract.claim: The fast choice for going deep or through rock: one call digs the whole job at body speed instead of one break_block per call. stairs_down mines the three cells ahead and below each step (a walkable 1-wide staircase, never straight down); steep_down mines four and drops two blocks per step (no fall damage, a third fewer blocks per level, but not walkable back up); stairs_up the two ahead and the jump headroom, tunnel a 1x2 passage. Heading: toward x/z when given (the larger axis first), else `heading`, else the way you face. The body selects the fastest hotbar tool, mines at vanilla speed, mines gravel that falls in, fills a one-block hole under the next step with a carried filler (cobblestone, dirt...), and plugs an opening it made onto lava. Like a player digging the repeated pattern, it handles on its own what needs no decision: a cave beside the stairs is passed and listed; water trickling into the cut is sealed with a carried block (up to 6 blocks a step); an open floor under the next step is followed sideways along the cave wall (it turns, never back up its own stairs), with no wall left it drops onto seen ground within 7 blocks (at most 4 fall damage, only when health stays 14 or more), else it crosses the cave top at its level (a carried block placed as the floor where open, up to 12 steps) until rock is under the next step again; `throughCaves:false` stops at the first cave instead. It stops and returns the facts (position, blocks mined, ores seen, tool uses left, caves passed, drops, water sealed) with: DIG_GOAL_REACHED, DIG_LIMIT_REACHED (maxBlocks), LAVA_AHEAD (seen or heard at the next cells; it never breaks into lava), WATER_AHEAD (more water than a few blocks seal: a lake, aquifer or the sea, or the eyes under water), CAVE_OPENING (a cave under the step it could not follow, drop into or cross), FALLING_BLOCKS, HOSTILE_NEAR (a hostile in sight within 12 blocks), DAMAGE_TAKEN, LOW_HEALTH (8 or less), LOW_FOOD (6 or less), NO_TOOL or TOOL_WORN (2 uses or fewer left; a second pickaxe in the hotbar is used next), INVENTORY_FULL, UNBREAKABLE, NO_FLOOR, DIG_STUCK. After a stop, deal with its cause and call dig_to again with the same target (another heading after a lava or cave stop). Cancel it like any action. Measured with an iron pickaxe: about 60 blocks a minute; steep_down about 2 s per level in stone and 2.5 s in deepslate, stairs_down about 3 s per level; surface to y-55 took 4-9 minutes of digging in 2-4 calls on most measured spots (about 3.5 s per level with its own turns and crossings), the usual stop a mob in sight. A full descent wears out about one iron pickaxe (about 250 blocks), so carry a spare.

contract.claim: Without aim fields the bow aims as a practised archer does: it turns to the middle of the target's visible body (the target may be outside your view if nothing blocks the line; you turn to it), leads a moving target (the flying dragon too) by its seen motion over the arrow's flight, holds above that point by the arrow's drop for this draw, re-aims while drawing at a moving target, then releases. Omit aim fields for crystals and the dragon alike; the result gives the aim point used. `trackTarget:true` also re-aims at a still target while drawing. `aimX`/`aimY`/`aimZ` instead fix one world point you choose (all three together, not with trackTarget; the bow adds nothing to it), and the result says where that point's arc reaches the target's range. A target past the bow's reach fails `RANGED_TARGET_OUT_OF_REACH`; one behind blocks that stop arrows fails `TARGET_OBSTRUCTED` naming the block (iron bars and glass panes are see-through but stop arrows). After release the bow watches your arrow for up to 3 s, as you would, and its message says how it ended: struck the target (it flashed hurt, or it broke), bounced off a perched dragon, or missed with the closest pass in blocks above/below and left/right of the target's centre plus the vanilla scatter at that range (every arrow leaves up to 1 block per 58 blocks off the aim each way, so a pass within scatter says nothing about the aim), stuck in a named block, or lost from sight. With a held pearl, snowball or egg, inspect first via use_item `mode:"inspect"` with the same aim, then choose whether to throw. This aims and uses once, reporting throwPreview; drawDurationMs applies only to bows. `footing:false` or `unknown_terrain` means the projectile may land without support (void/fall); the result's landing fields are authoritative predicted facts.

- In lava, held jump applies upward input every tick; releasing it sinks. Looking up and sprinting do not give water's sprint-swim speed in lava. player.exits lists known landings within 3 horizontal blocks, up to 3 above: direction, horizontal distance, upN/downN, Nlava, Ngap, unseen, coordinates. up1 is a jump; higher landings require rising first and do not certify a route. If none is nearby, it recalls one nearest remembered landing, including the way you walked (30 s memory); other seen terrain lasts 10 s. remembered Ns is its age, not a current guarantee. Empty exits means none known, not no possible shore. Lava hides what is behind it.
- An action that walks into lava or catches fire stops with IN_LAVA or ON_FIRE and the same exits. hurtBy names what last hurt you; lavaSeen lists lava you saw within 4 blocks in the last 30 s that is out of view. lavaFlow {from, at, inS} is seen lava flowing toward you: the lava it spreads from, the cell of yours it reaches and in about how many seconds.
- mine refuses a block with lava heard or seen beside it (LAVA_BEHIND) unless acceptLavaRisk:true. A block placed in the gap stops a flow.
- Magma blocks hurt while you stand on them unless you sneak.
